//: Lighthouse CI — mobile. Budgets guard the five metrics we care about.
The numbers are NOT the current values. They are the current values with
headroom, because a GitHub runner is a shared two-core box that is both
slower and far noisier than a developer machine, and a budget set at the
measured value is a build that fails on a bad afternoon rather than on a
regression. Measured median-of-3 against the built output at the time of
Timing budgets are roughly 1.6x those, so a 60% regression fails and drift
does not. CLS and TBT are absolute instead: 0.1 is the Core Web Vitals
'good' boundary, and both sites sit near zero, so those catch a real fault
rather than tracking a moving baseline.
Runs against the built static output, not a deploy. That keeps the check
deterministic and available on every PR, at the cost of not seeing CDN
headers or edge latency — those are covered by the Netlify checks.
